items.t: Head gasket leak and coolant loss
items.note: Usually covered by the powertrain warranty on these young cars. One owner was quoted almost $4,000 after the warranty ran out.

items.t: Engine stalls when coming to a stop (recall)
Fuel pump can break and stall the engine (recall)
Fuel line connector can leak under the hood (recall)
items.job: Replace fuel supply line and connector (recall 21V-651)

items.t: Hesitation or lurching when pulling away
items.note: Usually free under warranty. Parts cost extra if a sensor or fuel part is found faulty.

items.t: Slow, jerky dual-clutch response on AWD models
items.note: Usually free under warranty. Hardware repairs to the dual-clutch unit cost far more.

items.t: Loss of power with EPC and check engine lights
items.job: Diagnose and replace faulty engine sensor (such as boost or crankshaft sensor)
items.note: Wiring harness or fuel system faults can cost more.

items.t: Rear brakes wear out early and grind
items.job: Replace rear brake pads and rotors
items.note: CarComplaints lists a typical cost of about $800. Ask about warranty coverage for early pad wear.

items.t: Infotainment screen goes blank or reboots

items.job: Diagnose parasitic drain and replace 12V battery
items.note: YourMechanic estimates about $780 for a Taos battery replacement; shops charge up to about $1,390.

items.t: A/C blows warm from refrigerant leak
items.job: Find and repair A/C leak and recharge
items.note: A failed compressor costs much more. RepairPal lists A/C diagnosis at $140-$206 and a recharge at $344-$455.

items.job: Replace windshield wiper motor or control part
items.note: Based on RepairPal's wiper motor estimate ($617-$682). A sensor or software fix may cost less, and warranty may cover it.

items.job: Software update and instrument panel replacement as needed (recall 26V-185)

items.t: Fuel pressure sensor can pull loose in a crash (recall)
items.job: Install fuel pressure sensor harness extension (recall 26V-258)
